title: cold-kv-sojourn-eviction-watermark-probe-and-graceful-preempt-framework
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Introduce a conservative, low-latency preemption and fairness framework for continuous batching that explicitly accounts for KV cache residency (hot vs cold sojourns) and GPU memory fragmentation. Goals: reduce tail latency regressions for high-priority tenants, bound customer impact when eviction is necessary, and avoid repeated cold-start churn for recently accessed KV entries.
acceptance_criteria: New preemptor can preempt low-priority slices with <p99 latency regression of high-priority slices kept within configured SLO delta (default 15%)
Eviction watermark probe reduces repeated cold KV fetches for the same tenant by >= 40% in synthetic replay workload
GPU memory defragmentation windows and soft-resume hysteresis reduce OOM interruption rate by >= 30% under mixed workload stress
Automated e2e test covering tenant with heavy KV working set being preempted and resumed without losing more than 10% of local cache hit-rate
Telemetry surfaces: tenant-level preempt counts, kv-eviction-watermark events, cold-sojourn duration histogram, resume-success/failure ratio

notes: Motivation: existing preemption strategies aggressively evict KV entries causing repeated cold fetches and higher aggregate token cost. We need a middle ground between strict SLO preemption and tenant cache stability.

Key concept: eviction-watermark-probe = a lightweight periodic probe that measures whether evicting a tenant's KV slab will likely cause >X ms additional latency due to cold sojourn (based on recent locality and access cadence).

Design trade-offs considered: (1) Conservative probes reduce eviction aggressiveness but may degrade fairness under extreme load. (2) Aggressive eviction improves overall throughput but increases tail latency for a subset of tenants. Default policy leans conservative with config knobs for enterprise tiers.
Telemetry plan: emit "kv_probe_score" (0..1) per slab, "eviction_candidate" events with reason codes, and a tenant-level "grace_tokens" counter that gates preemption frequency.
Interoperability: should be compatible with existing canary-fit/fallback model routing. If model variant lacks local cache semantics, probe falls back to static heuristics.
Operational knobs: probe window length, probe weight multiplier for SLO-critical tenants, grace token refill rate, defrag window schedule (prefer low-traffic windows).
Security: no plaintext tenant data is used by probes; only access metadata and anonymized cardinalities. Will request security_review before release to Private customers.
